questions.question: North Dakota's land is organized into three landscape regions. From east to west, they are:
questions.correctAnswer: The Red River Valley, the Drift Prairie, and the Missouri Plateau
distractors: The Badlands, the Sandhills, and the Great Lakes Plain
The Red River Valley, the Black Hills, and the Missouri Plateau
The Drift Prairie, the Ozark Plateau, and the Red River Valley
questions.explanation: The three regions step upward from east to west: the flat Red River Valley along the Minnesota border, the rolling Drift Prairie in the center, and the higher, drier Missouri Plateau in the west.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Three steps climb west across the state.

img.scene: Three framed landscape panels side by side on a classroom wall: a flat green farm valley, rolling grassy hills with small ponds, and dry rugged buttes. Exactly three panels. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Three steps climb west across the state.
img.title: THREE LANDSCAPE REGIONS

questions.question: The Red River Valley is some of the flattest farmland on Earth because it was once:
questions.correctAnswer: The floor of glacial Lake Agassiz
distractors: The bed of an ancient ocean reef
A lava field smoothed by volcanoes
A desert flattened by wind
questions.explanation: As the glaciers melted, enormous Lake Agassiz covered the valley. When it drained, it left a nearly level lake bed of rich dark soil - which is why the valley floods spread so wide and farms run so flat.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A vanished lake left the flat valley floor.

img.scene: A vast flat green valley with a winding river and patchwork farms under a huge sky. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: A vanished lake left the flat valley floor.
img.title: THE LAKE THAT LEFT A VALLEY

questions.question: The river that forms North Dakota's entire eastern border, flowing north toward Canada, is the:
questions.correctAnswer: Red River of the North
distractors: Missouri River
James River
Souris River
questions.explanation: The Red River of the North flows north along the Minnesota border past Fargo and Grand Forks, eventually reaching Lake Winnipeg and Hudson Bay - one of the few major U.S. rivers that flows north.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Red runs north along the east edge.

img.scene: A wide muddy river flowing through flat farmland toward a distant northern horizon at sunrise. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: The Red runs north along the east edge.
img.title: THE NORTH-FLOWING RIVER

questions.question: The Missouri Plateau's most famous landscape, with layered buttes and eroded gullies in western North Dakota, is called the:
questions.correctAnswer: Badlands
distractors: Drift Prairie
Turtle Mountain
Pembina Gorge
questions.explanation: Wind and water carved the soft rock of the Missouri Plateau into the Badlands along the Little Missouri River - the landscape Theodore Roosevelt called 'as fantastic as the moon' country and where his ranching years changed him.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Erosion carved the Badlands' layered hills.

img.scene: Layered red, tan and gray buttes and eroded gullies in dry western rangeland under bright sun. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Erosion carved the Badlands' layered hills.
img.title: THE BADLANDS

questions.question: The rolling hills and thousands of small wetlands across central North Dakota were left behind by:
questions.correctAnswer: Glaciers that dropped drift - rock, gravel and sand - as they melted
distractors: Volcanic eruptions that dotted the plains
Rivers that dug evenly spaced ponds
Wind that piled the land into dunes
questions.explanation: The Drift Prairie takes its name from glacial drift. Melting ice dropped uneven debris and stranded ice blocks that melted into 'prairie pothole' wetlands, now famous waterfowl breeding habitat.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Melting ice dropped the drift and potholes.

img.scene: Rolling green grassland hills dotted with many small round ponds reflecting the sky. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Melting ice dropped the drift and potholes.
img.title: DRIFT AND PRAIRIE POTHOLES

questions.question: Garrison Dam on the Missouri River created North Dakota's largest lake, named for the Hidatsa guide of Lewis and Clark. That lake is:
questions.correctAnswer: Lake Sakakawea
distractors: Devils Lake
Lake Oahe
Lake Ashtabula
questions.explanation: Completed in 1953, Garrison Dam backed the Missouri up into Lake Sakakawea, one of the largest artificial lakes in the United States, named for Sakakawea, who joined the Lewis and Clark expedition at the Knife River villages.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The big dam lake carries her name.

img.scene: A huge blue reservoir stretching between dry bluffs behind a long earthen dam. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: The big dam lake carries her name.
img.title: LAKE SAKAKAWEA

questions.question: North Dakota's highest point, White Butte, rises in which landscape region?
questions.correctAnswer: The Missouri Plateau, in the southwest
distractors: The Red River Valley, near Fargo
The Drift Prairie, near Devils Lake
The Turtle Mountain, on the northern border
questions.explanation: White Butte, about 3,506 feet above sea level in Slope County, stands in the rugged Missouri Plateau country of the southwest - the high, dry end of the state's east-to-west climb.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The highest ground stands in the west.

img.scene: A single pale flat-topped butte rising above dry grassland in golden evening light. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: The highest ground stands in the west.
img.title: WHITE BUTTE, THE HIGH POINT

questions.question: A geographer explaining why Devils Lake keeps threatening the city of Devils Lake would point out that the lake:
questions.correctAnswer: Sits in a closed basin with no natural river outlet, so in wet cycles the water has nowhere to drain
distractors: Is fed by an underground river from Canada
Is drained by the Red River every spring
Was dug as a reservoir that engineers forgot to finish
questions.explanation: Devils Lake occupies a closed basin: water flows in from chains of prairie lakes but no river carries it out. Across the wet cycle that began in the 1990s the lake more than doubled in size, flooding farms, roads and shoreline homes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A lake with no outlet can only rise.

img.scene: A broad lake lapping at a raised gravel road with farm fields flooded on both sides. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: A lake with no outlet can only rise.
img.title: THE LAKE WITH NO OUTLET

questions.question: North Dakota's climate is best described as continental. For a student in Fargo, that means:
questions.correctAnswer: Very cold winters and warm summers, with most precipitation falling in the warmer months and less rain toward the drier west
distractors: Mild winters and cool, rainy summers all year
Hot, humid weather in every season
Equal rainfall in every part of the state
questions.explanation: Far from any ocean, North Dakota swings between extremes: subzero winters, hot summers, and a rainfall gradient that fades from roughly wetter east to semi-arid west - the pattern that splits the state between farming and ranching country.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: No ocean nearby means big swings.

img.scene: A split seasonal scene: snow-covered farmstead on one side, the same farmstead in green summer wheat on the other. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: No ocean nearby means big swings.
img.title: A CONTINENTAL CLIMATE

questions.question: The International Peace Garden, a park shared by the United States and Canada, sits on the border near Dunseith. It symbolizes North Dakota's identity as the:
questions.correctAnswer: Peace Garden State
distractors: Mount Rushmore State
Land of 10,000 Lakes
Cornhusker State
questions.explanation: Dedicated in 1932, the International Peace Garden straddles the North Dakota-Manitoba border to celebrate the long unfortified friendship between the two nations - and gave North Dakota its nickname, the Peace Garden State.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A garden on the border named the state.

img.scene: Formal flower gardens and a calm reflecting pool stretching toward a distant border monument. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: A garden on the border named the state.
img.title: THE PEACE GARDEN STATE

questions.question: The largest city in North Dakota, a Red River Valley hub for farm machinery, health care and a state university, is:
questions.correctAnswer: Fargo
distractors: Bismarck
Grand Forks
Minot
questions.explanation: Fargo, on the Red River across from Moorhead, Minnesota, is the state's largest city and its eastern commercial engine. Bismarck, the capital, sits farther west on the Missouri River.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fargo is biggest; Bismarck is capital.

img.tip: T-Rexy says: Fargo is biggest; Bismarck is capital.
img.title: FARGO, THE LARGEST CITY

questions.question: The state capital, Bismarck, was placed where it is mainly because of its position:
questions.correctAnswer: On the Missouri River, where the railroad reached and crossed the river
distractors: At the exact geographic center of the state
Beside the state's largest gold mine
On the Canadian border for trade defense
questions.explanation: Bismarck grew where the Northern Pacific Railroad met the Missouri River in 1873; the crossing made it a river-and-rail hub, and in 1883 it became capital of Dakota Territory, then of the state.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Rail meets river at the capital.

img.scene: A railroad bridge crossing a wide river toward a small capital city with a tall art deco tower. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Rail meets river at the capital.
img.title: CAPITAL ON THE MISSOURI

questions.question: The wooded, lake-dotted highland along the Canadian border, home of the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa, is the:
questions.correctAnswer: Turtle Mountain
distractors: Knife River bluffs
Killdeer Mountains
Pembina Hills only
questions.explanation: The Turtle Mountain is a forested plateau of hills and lakes straddling the Manitoba border - a green island above the prairie and the homeland of the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Indians.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A forested island rises on the border.

img.scene: A forested green plateau of hills and small lakes rising above flat surrounding prairie. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: A forested island rises on the border.
img.title: TURTLE MOUNTAIN

questions.question: A rancher west of the Missouri River and a wheat farmer in the Red River Valley farm different landscapes mainly because, moving west across North Dakota:
questions.correctAnswer: Rainfall decreases and the land becomes higher and rougher, favoring grazing over intensive cropping
distractors: The soil becomes richer and wetter with every mile
Winters disappear and crops grow year-round
The land sinks below the eastern valley floor
questions.explanation: The settlement map follows the climate map: the wet, flat east supports intensive row crops and wheat, the Drift Prairie mixes farming and grazing, and the dry Missouri Plateau is mostly ranch country broken by irrigated river bottoms.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Drier and rougher west means ranching.

img.scene: A cattle herd grazing dry western rangeland with buttes behind, wheat combines far in the green distance. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Drier and rougher west means ranching.
img.title: WHY THE WEST RANCHES

questions.question: The Missouri River crosses North Dakota on a long journey. Its course through the state runs:
questions.correctAnswer: In from Montana in the northwest, southeast past Bismarck, and out into South Dakota
distractors: In from Minnesota, north past Fargo, and out into Canada
In from South Dakota, west past Medora, and out into Wyoming
Only along the Canadian border from west to east
questions.explanation: The Missouri enters North Dakota from Montana, is dammed at Garrison to form Lake Sakakawea, flows past Bismarck, and leaves into South Dakota toward Lake Oahe - the state's great western water highway since the days of the fur trade.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: In from Montana, out to South Dakota.

img.scene: A great river curving through bluffs and cottonwood bottoms across an open plains map-like landscape. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: In from Montana, out to South Dakota.
img.title: THE MISSOURI'S PATH

questions.question: North Dakota shares its northern border with which two Canadian provinces?
questions.correctAnswer: Saskatchewan and Manitoba
distractors: Alberta and Ontario
Manitoba and Ontario
British Columbia and Saskatchewan
questions.explanation: The 49th parallel forms the border: Saskatchewan lies northwest of North Dakota and Manitoba northeast, which is why trade, weather systems and the Turtle Mountain all tie the state to the Canadian plains.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Saskatchewan west, Manitoba east, up north.

img.scene: A long straight prairie border with wheat fields stretching to the horizon and a small border marker. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Saskatchewan west, Manitoba east, up north.
img.title: NEIGHBORS TO THE NORTH

questions.question: A student mapping North Dakota's water would place the Sheyenne and James rivers in which drainage?
questions.correctAnswer: The Hudson Bay drainage, because they eventually flow north through the Red River system
distractors: The Gulf of Mexico drainage, through the Missouri and Mississippi
The Pacific drainage, through the Columbia
No drainage - all North Dakota rivers stay in closed lakes
questions.explanation: Eastern North Dakota drains north: the Sheyenne joins the Red River and the James loops down and back to join the Red system, all bound for Hudson Bay. The Missouri River system in the west and south drains the other way, to the Gulf of Mexico - a continental divide crosses the state.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: East drains north; the Missouri drains south.

img.scene: Two river systems splitting across a plains landscape, one flowing north, one flowing south. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: East drains north; the Missouri drains south.
img.title: A DIVIDE CROSSES THE STATE

questions.question: The Theodore Roosevelt National Park preserves Badlands country near Medora because that landscape:
questions.correctAnswer: Shaped Theodore Roosevelt's conservation outlook during his 1880s ranching years there
distractors: Was the site of his birth in the Dakota Territory
Holds the only fossil beds he ever studied
Was where he signed the statehood proclamation
questions.explanation: Roosevelt came to Dakota Territory in 1883 to hunt, then ranched near Medora. The hard ranching life and the vanishing frontier wildlife he witnessed there drove the conservation ethic of his presidency; the park's three units honor that connection.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Badlands taught a president conservation.

img.scene: Painted canyon badlands with wild horses grazing on a grassy bench above the gullies. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: The Badlands taught a president conservation.
img.title: ROOSEVELT'S BADLANDS

questions.question: Since about 2006, towns like Williston and Watford City in the northwest have grown explosively. On a thematic map, that population change would be explained by:
questions.correctAnswer: Oil development in the Bakken formation of the Williston Basin
distractors: A new seaport on Lake Sakakawea
The return of the bonanza farms
A gold rush in the Turtle Mountain
questions.explanation: Horizontal drilling and hydraulic fracturing unlocked the Bakken shale, and the Williston Basin boomed: workers poured in, northwestern towns doubled in size, and a farming-and-ranching corner of the state became an energy landscape of rigs, housing camps and new roads.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Bakken boom redrew the northwest.

img.scene: Oil pumpjacks and a drilling rig among wheat fields near a fast-growing small town at dusk. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: The Bakken boom redrew the northwest.
img.title: BOOM IN THE NORTHWEST

questions.question: Which pairing of city and river is correct on a map of North Dakota?
questions.correctAnswer: Grand Forks - Red River of the North
distractors: Minot - Missouri River
Fargo - James River
Bismarck - Red River of the North
questions.explanation: Grand Forks stands where the Red Lake River joins the Red River of the North - the junction that made it a trading point and the site of the devastating 1997 flood. Minot is on the Souris, Fargo on the Red but not the James, and Bismarck on the Missouri.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Grand Forks guards the Red's forks.

img.scene: Two rivers joining at a confluence beside a small downtown with a high flood wall. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Grand Forks guards the Red's forks.
img.title: WHERE THE RIVERS MEET

questions.question: The rich black soil of the Red River Valley is especially famous for growing:
questions.correctAnswer: Sugar beets and potatoes, alongside wheat and soybeans
distractors: Cotton and rice
Coffee and citrus
Cranberries and maple sugar
questions.explanation: The flat, stone-free, nutrient-rich lake-bed soil, drained by ditches and tile, produces top national harvests of sugar beets and potatoes as well as wheat, soybeans and dry beans - the valley is one of America's great food bowls.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lake-bed soil grows beets and potatoes.

img.scene: Endless flat fields of green sugar beets with red potato harvesters working a distant row. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Lake-bed soil grows beets and potatoes.
img.title: VALLEY OF BEETS AND POTATOES

questions.question: Prairie pothole wetlands matter far beyond North Dakota because they:
questions.correctAnswer: Produce a large share of North America's ducks and other waterfowl each year
distractors: Supply drinking water to the Great Lakes
Stop tornadoes from forming on the plains
Are the only wetlands left anywhere in the world
questions.explanation: The glaciated pothole region - the 'duck factory' - breeds roughly half of North America's waterfowl in good years, which is why wetland drainage or protection in central North Dakota is a continental conservation issue, not just a farm issue.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Potholes are the continent's duck factory.

img.scene: A small round wetland crowded with ducks taking flight at dawn over grassland. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Potholes are the continent's duck factory.
img.title: THE DUCK FACTORY

questions.question: Early settlers called the Red River Valley's biggest farms 'bonanza farms.' A thematic map of settlement would show them concentrated in the valley chiefly because:
questions.correctAnswer: The railroad sold huge tracts of flat, fertile land that could be farmed profitably at very large scale with machinery
distractors: The valley had the state's only supply of timber
Federal law required all farms over a thousand acres to locate there
The valley's hills protected crops from every flood
questions.explanation: In the 1870s and 1880s the Northern Pacific sold land in enormous blocks; investors like the Dalrymple interests ran wheat farms of thousands of acres with steam-powered machinery - proof that plains wheat farming paid, which pulled settlers in behind them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Railroad land plus flat wheat soil equaled bonanzas.

img.scene: A vast flat wheat field with rows of horse-drawn and early steam farm machines in vintage style. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Railroad land plus flat wheat soil equaled bonanzas.
img.title: BONANZA FARMS

questions.question: A student is asked which single physical feature most shaped where North Dakota's first towns appeared. The strongest answer is:
questions.correctAnswer: Rivers - the Missouri and the Red supplied water, transport and trading-post sites long before railroads
distractors: Mountain passes through the Rockies
Natural deep-water harbors on the coast
Gold deposits in the western hills
questions.explanation: Pembina, the fur posts on the Missouri, and the river towns all began on water: rivers carried furs, settlers and supplies, watered livestock and powered early mills. Railroads later followed and reinforced the same river corridors.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: First the rivers, then the rails.

img.scene: A historic trading post with stockade walls beside a wide river, canoes and wagons nearby. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: First the rivers, then the rails.
img.title: TOWNS FOLLOWED RIVERS

questions.question: Comparing the state's regions, which statement is most accurate?
questions.correctAnswer: The Red River Valley is the lowest, flattest and wettest; the Missouri Plateau is the highest, roughest and driest
distractors: The Missouri Plateau is the lowest and wettest region
All three regions have nearly identical land and rainfall
The Drift Prairie is a desert of sand dunes
questions.explanation: North Dakota stair-steps upward to the west: from the Lake Agassiz floor at under 1,000 feet, across the rolling Drift Prairie, to White Butte at about 3,506 feet - while rainfall declines in the same direction. Land, climate and livelihood all change together.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Low and wet in the east, high and dry west.

img.scene: A cross-section landscape rising in steps from a flat green valley to dry western buttes. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Low and wet in the east, high and dry west.
img.title: THE WESTWARD STAIR-STEP

questions.question: Before North Dakota had a state or county government, the Mandan, Hidatsa, Arikara, Sioux and Chippewa peoples governed themselves. In civics terms, tribal nations today are:
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereign governments that relate to the United States government-to-government
distractors: Private cultural clubs with no governing power
Departments inside county government
Corporations owned by the state
questions.explanation: Tribal sovereignty predates the United States: the federally recognized tribes in North Dakota govern their own citizens and lands, make their own laws and courts, and deal with Washington as governments - a status treaties and the U.S. Constitution's framework recognize.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tribes are governments, not clubs.

img.scene: A tribal council chamber with flags and a circle of seated leaders in discussion, dignified and calm. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Tribes are governments, not clubs.
img.title: SOVEREIGN TRIBAL GOVERNMENTS

questions.question: At the state heritage center, a student stops at a display of tribal government seals - one seal for each federally recognized tribal nation headquartered within the state's borders. When the display is complete, the student has counted:
questions.correctAnswer: Five - including the Mandan, Hidatsa and Arikara Nation, the Standing Rock Sioux Tribe, the Spirit Lake Tribe, the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa, and the Sisseton Wahpeton Oyate
distractors: Two
Nine
Twelve
questions.explanation: The seals belong to the Mandan, Hidatsa and Arikara Nation (Fort Berthold), the Standing Rock Sioux Tribe, the Spirit Lake Tribe, the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Indians, and the Sisseton Wahpeton Oyate (Lake Traverse) - five governments in all.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Five tribal nations call North Dakota home.

img.scene: A map-like landscape with five distinct reservation homelands shown as five separate council lodges across plains and lakes country, no labels. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Five tribal nations call North Dakota home.
img.title: FIVE TRIBAL NATIONS

questions.question: North Dakota's state constitution was written at a convention in the summer of 1889 in which city?
questions.correctAnswer: Bismarck
distractors: Fargo
Yankton
Grand Forks
questions.explanation: Delegates met in Bismarck in July 1889 to write the constitution under which North Dakota entered the Union that November. Unusually, the state still operates under that original 1889 constitution, amended many times since.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The 1889 convention met in Bismarck.

img.tip: T-Rexy says: The 1889 convention met in Bismarck.

questions.question: North Dakota became a state on November 2, 1889. Its statehood was unusual because:
questions.correctAnswer: It entered the Union the same day as South Dakota, after one Dakota Territory was split in two
distractors: It was admitted before it had a constitution
It entered as two separate states that later merged
It was the last territory ever admitted
questions.explanation: Dakota Territory, created in 1861, was divided along what is now the state line, and Presidents' proclamations admitted North and South Dakota together - legend says the papers were shuffled so no one knows which was signed first. North Dakota is counted as the 39th state.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Two Dakotas, one birthday.

img.scene: A crowd celebrating outside a frontier capitol in 1889 with flags and a brass band, winter light. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Two Dakotas, one birthday.

questions.question: The lawmaking branch of North Dakota government, which meets in regular session in odd-numbered years, is called the:
questions.correctAnswer: Legislative Assembly
distractors: General Court
State Congress
House of Burgesses
questions.explanation: North Dakota's legislature is the Legislative Assembly - a Senate and a House of Representatives that meet for up to 80 days every two years, a citizen-legislature design that assumes members hold other jobs back home.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Assembly makes the laws.

img.scene: A modern legislative chamber with rows of desks in a semicircle inside an art deco capitol. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: The Assembly makes the laws.
img.title: THE LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY

questions.question: In North Dakota's government, the three branches divide power so that laws are made, enforced and interpreted by separate hands. The branch that interprets laws and settles disputes under them is the:
questions.correctAnswer: Judicial branch, headed by the state Supreme Court
distractors: Executive branch, headed by the governor
Legislative branch, headed by the Senate
County commissions of the 53 counties
questions.explanation: The state Supreme Court's five justices, elected to ten-year terms, head the judicial branch of district and municipal courts. Separation of powers keeps judging apart from the governor who enforces laws and the assembly that writes them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Courts interpret; others make and enforce.

img.tip: T-Rexy says: Courts interpret; others make and enforce.

questions.question: North Dakota is famous among civics students for one election rule: it is the only state that:
questions.correctAnswer: Does not require citizens to register before voting
distractors: Lets sixteen-year-olds vote in state elections
Elects its governor every single year
Has no secret ballot
questions.explanation: Since 1951 North Dakota has had no voter registration. Eligible citizens simply show identification at the polls - a system the state keeps because of its small, stable communities, and one no other state copies.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Show up with ID - no registration list.

questions.question: Fed up with distant corporations controlling grain prices, North Dakota farmers in 1915 organized a political movement that swept state elections the next year. It was the:
questions.correctAnswer: Nonpartisan League
distractors: Know-Nothing Party
Liberty League
Farm Bureau Federation
questions.explanation: Founded by organizer A. C. Townley, the Nonpartisan League enrolled farmers as members, endorsed candidates in party primaries, and in 1916 elected Governor Lynn Frazier and a legislative majority - then rewrote the state's economic rules within a few years.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Farmers organized and took the statehouse.

img.scene: Farmers in 1910s dress signing membership cards at a crowded rural meeting hall. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
img.tip: T-Rexy says: Farmers organized and took the statehouse.

questions.question: Two governing tools the populist era gave North Dakota citizens let voters act directly on laws. The initiative lets citizens:
questions.correctAnswer: Propose a law or constitutional amendment themselves and put it to a statewide vote after gathering petition signatures
distractors: Remove any judge whose ruling they dislike
Veto a bill before the governor sees it
Elect the legislature one member at a time
questions.explanation: Under the initiative, citizens draft a measure, gather the required signatures of qualified voters, and the proposal goes on the ballot - lawmaking that bypasses the Legislative Assembly entirely, a Nonpartisan League-era reform North Dakotans still use.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Citizens can write the ballot themselves.

img.scene: Citizens gathering petition signatures on clipboards outside a county courthouse. No readable text, no words, no letters, no numbers anywhere in the image.
